why: The identity tint stops being applied per EMISSION, so a decal keeps whatever colour it was built with. Decals are pooled (`pool.pop() ?? makeDecal()`), so the visible defect is not 'no colour' -- it is a player inheriting ANOTHER player's tint the moment the pool turns over, which on a busy board is most marks. It looks like a working feature in a screenshot of a fresh round and wrong in play, and no assertion on `treadColorFor` alone can see it, since that function stays correct. Caught by the real-emit-path case and by the pool-turnover case that expires one player's marks before the other prints into them. Scoped to tread-trails.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only. The replacement is `void colorHex;` rather than an empty string: the manifest validator requires a non-empty `replace` (lib.mjs, "'replace' must be a non-empty string"), and a no-op that still consumes the parameter expresses the deletion without leaving an unused-argument diagnostic behind it.
killedBy: tread trails carry their owner identity in VS (issue #284) does not let a POOLED decal keep the previous owner colour
tread trails carry their owner identity in VS (issue #284) prints each owner its own colour through the real emit path
